museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research
title: Centre of Visual Arts and Research: Masterpieces
subtitle: Harbours, plants, monuments and sketches in the Centre of Visual Arts and Research collection, Nicosia.
introduction:
A harbour store, a flowering stem and a quickly drawn statue record Cyprus at very different scales. This selection from Nicosia's Centre of Visual Arts and Research brings them together without asking them to provide a single, complete image of the island. Some works preserve named buildings; others give only a broad location. Several have no securely identified artist.

Captions matter particularly here. A written place and date can anchor a watercolour in a journey, while a traveller's historical label may require correction. The pictures are evidence of how particular people looked and recorded, not transparent windows onto an unchanged Cyprus. Read the image and its accompanying words as related but distinct records.
visitNote: These are collection records from the Centre of Visual Arts and Research in Nicosia. Works on paper rotate, and the selection is not a guaranteed display route. Historical place names and captions belong to the source objects; they do not establish current access or settle present-day geography. Source watermarks are retained.

books.title: Our Home in Cyprus
books.author: Esmé Scott-Stevenson (1880)
books.access: Free digitized English edition through Google Books; availability and sign-in requirements can vary.
books.note: Scott-Stevenson, whose landscape appears in this guide, also wrote about living and travelling in Cyprus. Her book is a historical source shaped by a British colonial viewpoint. Read its descriptions alongside the pictures, asking whose activities and perspectives remain outside each account.

works.title: Saint George Xorinos, Famagusta
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The church rises behind trees and cultivated ground, so its stone walls belong to a setting still occupied by growth and use. Paths keep the foreground connected to the building. The view records more than a monument's outline: it preserves a particular arrangement around the monument, which should not be assumed to survive unchanged.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Portrait of Mrs Razzini
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: A name has survived for the sitter, though not for the painter. Her dark dress and light trim make the pose legible against the pale ground; the hands settle near the waist. That is enough for a close portrait description. It does not supply a profession, family history or temperament for Mrs Razzini.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Salt Lake, Cyprus
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The lake and sky spread in pale horizontal bands, interrupted by slender palms and stems. Those uprights help measure the openness without filling it. The sparse description is especially useful here: adding equal detail everywhere would make it harder to register the extent of the water and the distance between its edges.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Trees at Platres
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The descending slope is understood through changes in the density of trees. Darker trunks hold the near ground while hills carry the view farther away. An anonymous landscape can still preserve a specific spatial arrangement. The absence of an artist's name is a gap in its record, not a reason to invent a traveller behind it.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Carob Stores in Kyrenia Harbour
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The broad quay and waterfront stores give the harbour a working edge. Following the curve of the shore connects the buildings to the water they face. The title identifies carob storage, directing attention to an economic use that an attractive harbour view can otherwise make easy to overlook.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: From Pedoulas
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The place named in the title is represented by flowering stems rather than an extensive view. Branching joints, leaves and blossoms remain separate on the open sheet. This is another scale of travel record: a location may be remembered through something studied close at hand, without being reduced to a panorama or landmark.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: View towards Agia Irini Bay and Morphou
works.catalogueTitle: From the top of a mountain (Agia Irini Bay, Morphou)
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The high viewpoint arranges the land in successive distances: rough ground nearby, ridges farther out and the coastal plain leading toward the sea. The foreground gives the broad bands a physical scale. It is a view selected from a particular position, not a neutral map of all the territory named in its title.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: A Male Figure
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: A bent arm and a few folds give the lightly drawn body its organisation. The unfinished head and absent setting leave attention on the pose. There is little basis for identifying an emotion or an occasion. The drawing is useful precisely as a selective record, showing how few relations are needed to make a standing figure legible.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Ancient Artefact
works.license: The  Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The object's profile occupies only a small part of the sheet. Darker strokes distinguish one side, but the drawing does not provide the archaeological context that would identify its original use. Keeping the broad museum title respects that limit. A careful outline and an uncertain identification can coexist in the same record.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Ancient Female Statue
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The bent arms and hands near the chest repeat across the frontal torso, while the head receives less definition. Bakst selects a bodily arrangement from a sculptural object instead of supplying an exhaustive copy. That economy makes the drawing useful for comparing forms, though it cannot replace the fuller evidence of the statue itself.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Cyprus: Shaving a Priest
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The seated man is surrounded by other figures rather than isolated as the subject of a portrait. The caption identifies the service being performed; the loose interior and nearby objects leave much of its setting unresolved. The sheet records a social situation, but cannot establish every participant's identity or the exact circumstances of their meeting.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Salt Lake, Larnaca, with Stavrovouni
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: Water and a distant mountain occupy the view, while the inscription fixes a place and a day: 9 March 1938. Image and caption do different jobs. One arranges the visible distances; the other locates this stop in a sequence of travel. Together they make the watercolour more specific than a general impression of Cyprus.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: The Lighthouse, Kyrenia
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The tower is brought close enough for its masonry to register against the water, with a sailing vessel extending the harbour beyond it. Balfour's historical caption is part of the record, but its reference to an “old Roman” lighthouse should not be accepted as an archaeological dating. A traveller's label preserves an understanding, not necessarily a verified fact.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Bellapais Abbey
works.catalogueTitle: Abbey of Bella Paise - Kyrenia Built by Hugh IV, King of Cyprus 1324 March 1
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: Trees and the green slope surround the ruined arches, placing the abbey within a larger terrain. The mounted caption records Balfour's visit and his historical understanding of the site. Those are separable matters: the picture can establish how he represented the building without confirming every statement written beneath it.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Flowers
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: Open flowers, buds and leaves give different stages of growth a place on one branching stem. The pale background keeps each junction available for examination. Unlike a bouquet arranged as a solid mass, this study relies on the spaces between parts, allowing a small plant to occupy the sheet without losing its individual structures.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Kyrenia
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: Fine lines establish buildings and masts while reflections carry some of their verticals into the water. The warm paper remains visible between the marks, contributing colour without a separate wash in every area. The harbour is therefore assembled partly through what is left untouched, rather than through an evenly filled surface.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Ruins at Amathus
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The irregular border encloses ruins, trees and small figures, with mountains opening beyond them. The museum's tentative association with Pars remains uncertain and should not become a confident signature in retelling. That qualification does not prevent discussion of the composition, where the human scale is held within a much larger landscape.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: The Mosque at Famagusta
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The Gothic building and its minaret occupy the same skyline. Their conjunction makes architectural change visible without requiring the earlier form to have disappeared. Small figures and lower structures keep the site inhabited rather than treating it as an isolated specimen. The watercolour records a particular historical view, not the site's present appearance.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: View from a Wooded Hilltop, Cyprus
works.catalogueTitle: View from a wooded hilltop, Cyprus
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: The trees' broad crowns provide the strongest shapes across the sheet; thinner trunks hold them above the low ground. Their spacing makes the hilltop recognisable as a place with intervals and openings rather than a continuous mass of green. The unknown artist's identity remains separate from what this arrangement allows the image to show.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

works.title: Ancient Statue
works.license: The Costas and Rita Severis Foundation holds or manages the copyright(s) of this item and its digital reproduction. If you need information about using this item, please send an email to [email protected]
works.description: Drawing and annotation share this small sheet from Bakst's 1921 visit. The frontal statue's pose is reduced to a few contours, including a hand held toward the chest. The CVAR connects his Cypriot studies with costume work, a reminder that a travel sketch can become material for later invention as well as a record of an encountered object.
works.museum: Centre of Visual Arts and Research

closingSections.title: A picture is one kind of record
paragraphs: Follow the object links for inscriptions and catalogue information, particularly when a building's name or attribution is uncertain. Present-day place names, access and condition need separate checking. The selection describes collection records rather than a current hanging, and permission to reproduce an image must be checked independently of permission to visit the museum.
